newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Rallies on refinery glitch.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Rallies on refinery glitch.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel markets rallied on Tuesday as Shell Singapore suffered technical problems at two of its secondary processing units and are seeking to cover gas oil shortages for mid-March, traders said.
The jet fuel market rose on continued pricing by a local trader of its cargo sales into Indonesia, traders said.
Shell has shut down half of its 82,000-barrel-per-day thermal gas oil unit since March 2 and will shut a 32,780-bpd hydrocracker on March 5, both for a week, due to technical problems.

Shell has sought gas oil since Monday raising its bid to $25.95 a barrel, from $25.60. The cargo sought is 220,000 barrels for March 19-23 lifting fob. A Dutch trader also bid at the same level for March 20-24 lifting.
Another European major, which has bought Shell's cargo recently at a 20-cent-per-barrel premium to Singapore quotes fob, offered the cargo at $26.45 for March 23-27 lifting fob.
Concerns over the refinery problems and tight prompt supplies forced up swaps values by 40 cents per barrel to be last quoted at $25.85/$25.95 for March.
The swaps jet fuel/gas oil regrade gained another 10 cents to be bid at $2.00, and the widening spread was also seen on the physical market.
A Singapore trader bought another 100,000-barrel jet cargo at $29.10 per barrel for March 19-23 lifting fob from a U.S. major. This was 60 cents over the cargo which the trader bought on Monday.
Taiwan has issued a tender to buy jet fuel for second-half April delivery, closing March 11.
Vietnam's Petrolimex is expected to issue its tender for second quarter delivery by end March, a Hanoi source said.
